heading: Growth is growing and already profitable. Hot tape is recent price. Cheap on operating profit is valuation. Conviction is analyst sentiment.

captions.strength: Hot tape — recent price, not a forecast.
captions.undervalued: Cheap on operating profit, not a quality grade.
captions.conviction: Analyst sentiment — strong-buy share and earnings revisions.

strength.name: Strength
strength.method: Hot tape — recent price, not a forecast. 60% 63-session return and 40% 252-session return among liquid names with a full QQQ calendar. The published list is the top 10% of that tape, at most 150 names.

growth.name: Growth
growth.method: Growing companies that already make money. Gates: quarterly revenue YoY ≥ 20%, TTM net income > 0, prior-year quarterly revenue ≥ $50M, ROE present. Rank: return on equity. Revenue growth is a gate, not a score. Six-month return versus QQQ is shown beside the rank; it is the tape, not the score. Every name that passes the gates is published; Growth is not cut to a top-10% shortlist.

undervalued.name: Cheap on operating profit
undervalued.method: Cheap on operating profit: TTM operating income / EV, where EV is equity market cap plus interest-bearing debt minus cash. Requires positive operating income, a consistent statement, net margin between -20% and 80% when reported, and cash plus debt on the same filing asset date. Names without EV are out. The published list is the top 10% of that set, at most 150 names. OI / equity cap is shown beside the rank so leverage is visible; it is not the score. Leases and NCI are not in EV. Generic OI / EV excludes banks, insurers, diversified financials, mortgage companies, and REITs because operating income and debt do not have the same economic meaning in those sectors.

conviction.name: Conviction
conviction.method: Analyst sentiment: 50% strong-buy-share percentile and 50% current-fiscal-year 30-day EPS-revision-breadth percentile among liquid names with at least 5 ratings and both valid inputs. Counts are dated by retrieval; Yahoo has no per-report publication time. The list is not point-in-time at the Friday price close unless a decision cutoff at or after retrieval is supplied. Strong-buy share is Strong Buy over all five labels, not Strong Buy plus Buy. The published list keeps the top 10% of that scored set, with a floor of 50 and cap of 150 (or all names if fewer than 50 qualify). Breadth is (up − down) / (up + down); no revisions is neutral zero, while missing coverage is excluded. One upward revision and ten upward revisions can have the same breadth: inspect the counts. Use this to prioritize research alongside valuation and fundamentals; it is not a win probability or a record of individual upgrades.
